item.title: Trump weighs in on LeBron James vs Michael Jordan debate: 'I only like people that like me'
item.description: President Donald Trump was asked who he thought was better, Michael Jordan or LeBron James, and Trump said he thought the Chicago Bulls legend was better.
item.content:encoded:
President Donald Trump has weighed in on one of basketball’s biggest debates: Who is better, LeBron James or Michael Jordan?

For Trump, the answer is easy. The president is all in on Jordan.

"Michael Jordan is a guy that's a friend of mine, play golf with him. He's a really good guy. And I think LeBron is, maybe he's a racist, but maybe he doesn't like Trump, I don't know. But I only like people that like me. So, I would say Michael Jordan all the way," Trump said at the Oval Office on Friday.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE SPORTS COVERAGE ON FOXNEWS.COM

Trump was asked the James vs. Jordan question because James announced Friday that he plans to sign with the Philadelphia 76ers. He will sign a two-year, $8 million contract, according to ESPN.

Jordan played in the NBA for 15 seasons, winning six titles in his career, all of which came with the Chicago Bulls. Jordan retired twice during his career, as he played baseball after the Bulls’ first three-peat during the 1993-94 season.

He returned during the 1994-95 season, and the Bulls began their second three-peat a year later during the 1995-96 season. Jordan then retired again, this time for three seasons, and spent the final two seasons of his career with the Washington Wizards.

In his career, Jordan averaged 30.1 points per game, the most in NBA history, along with 6.2 rebounds and 5.3 assists. The Basketball Hall of Famer made the All-Star team 14 times, won five MVPs, six NBA Finals MVPs, was a 10-time scoring champion, and made the All-Defensive Team nine times.

LEBRON JAMES MAKES NBA FREE AGENCY DECISION, ANNOUNCES PLANS TO SIGN WITH 76ERS

James is heading into his 24th season, his first with the 76ers. He spent the first seven years of his career with the Cleveland Cavaliers, and then signed with the Miami Heat to create "The Big 3" with Dwyane Wade and Chris Bosh.

James won the first two of his four NBA titles with the Heat in 2011-12 and 2012-13. After four seasons with the Heat, James returned home to Cleveland.

In his second stint with the Cavaliers, James led the Cavaliers to the title in 2015-16, completing a 3-1 series comeback over the Golden State Warriors. After four more seasons in Cleveland, James departed for the Los Angeles Lakers.

In eight seasons with the Lakers, James won one NBA title during the 2019-20 season. That championship was won in the bubble in Florida because of the COVID-19 pandemic.

James is the NBA’s leader in games played, points, most All-Star selections and All-NBA selections. He is the only player in NBA history to score more than 43,000 points and has the most 30-point games (700) of all time.

He has won the MVP award four times, is a 22-time All-Star, a 21-time All-NBA selection, a four-time Finals MVP and a six-time All-Defensive Team member.

In his career, he has averaged 26.8 points, 7.2 assists and 6.1 rebounds per game.

Both James and Jordan have incredible résumés, which has led to one of the most contentious debates in sports. But even with James’ résumé still growing, Trump’s answer is clear: Jordan all the way.

item.title: Buffalo Bills' latest edition to their new stadium is predictably (and painfully) on brand
item.description: A 20-foot broken folding table now stands in the concourse of Buffalo's new $2.1 billion Highmark Stadium as a tribute to Bills Mafia tailgate culture.
item.content:encoded:
The Buffalo Bills are in the final stages of unveiling their new, $2.1 billion stadium, and from the looks of it, it has all the bells and whistles any football fan could need.

When Highmark Stadium opens in time for the 2026 NFL season, it's sure to be one of the most state of the art venues in the league.

Two billion big ones can buy you a lot these days, but it's one of the latest editions to the Bills' new home — one that likely didn't cost a ton — that has everyone on the internet talking.

NY GOVERNOR KATHY HOCHUL TRIES TO GET BILLS CHANT GOING AT NEW STADIUM, COMPLETELY FAILS

No, it's not a 100-foot scoreboard or a retractable roof, but it is something that is instantly identifiable as a Buffalo staple, and after seeing it, I couldn't imagine the new stadium without it.

Is there anything that screams "Bills Culture" quite like a 20-foot broken folding table in the middle of the concourse of a multi-billion dollar stadium?

The answer, of course, is "no," and although it seems like a no-brainer in hindsight, whoever pitched this in the market meetings deserves a raise.

JOSH ALLEN RECALLS HIS ROLE IN BILLS' COACHING SEARCH, DETAILS JOE BRADY’S APPROACH TO NEW ROLE

For the uninitiated, the new ornament is an homage to "Bills Mafia," the crazed section of the Buffalo fanbase who is notorious for throwing themselves through folding tables at tailgates before the game (those tables may or may not also be on fire at times).

Some Debbie Downers on X are trying to clown the Bills for adding this to their new digs, but if you hate this then you don't love fun or football.

A broken folding table is woven into the fabric of the identity of the city; it's literally ingrained in the fanbase's DNA.

JOSH ALLEN SAYS HE WOULD BE 'VERY HONORED' TO PLAY FOR TEAM USA IN FLAG FOOTBALL AT 2028 OLYMPICS

As a Dolphins fan, I wish we had something that was so identifiable with our fanbase.

When I was in middle school, the Dolphins tried to do this whole rebrand as a place where celebrities would come and hang out.

They called a section of the stadium the "Orange Carpet," and got "local" A-listers who lived in the area like J-Lo and the Williams sisters to show up to games, but all it did was alienate the core fanbase (the losing didn't help).

It was right around that time that my dad and a lot of other longtime supporters stopped buying season tickets, and it's been kind of embarrassing to be a Fins fan ever since.

My point is that Buffalo is a real football town, and having a 20-foot piece of art dedicated to the people who show up every autumn and winter in sub-zero temperatures just to watch their team inevitably lose to the Chiefs in January is beautiful; it's poetic.

The fans love their Bills and the Bills love their fans, and that's what football is all about.

Long live Bills Mafia and long live the folding table statue.

item.title: Ben Affleck and Casey Affleck's mom, Chris Anne Affleck, dead at 83 after pancreatic cancer battle
item.description: Chris Anne Affleck was diagnosed with pancreatic cancer in December 2025 and given six months to live. Her obituary reveals a touching final wish.
item.content:encoded:
Ben Affleck and Casey Affleck's mom has died following a battle with cancer.

According to an obituary published in The Boston Globe on Friday, Christopher Anne Affleck, died peacefully in her sleep on June 2 at the age of 83.

The Hollywood Reporter reported she was diagnosed with pancreatic cancer in December 2025, and was given six months to live.

"Her greatest wish after her diagnosis, however, was to live to see her grandson graduate high school," the obituary reads. "She did so, attending with her family on May 31, 2026. She died peacefully, in her sleep, two days later."

HOLLYWOOD STARS WHO DIED IN 2026

Born in 1942 in New York City, Chris proved to be a great activist, teaching "literacy classes in Mississippi during Freedom Summer, marched against the Vietnam War, and reveled in 1960s counterculture."

She went on to become "one of the first Radcliffe women" to graduate from Harvard, and spent 35 years as a public school teacher.

"Every student, whether just arrived from Haiti or Cambridge upper crust, was a cherished citizen of her classroom republic, equal to each other and to herself," the obituary states.

After working as a teacher for over three decades, Chris retired in 2008, spending time volunteering for President Barack Obama during his campaign, traveling to Israel/Palestine and becoming an organizer for the Alliance for Water Justice in Palestine.

Chris welcomed Ben in 1972 and Casey in 1975, with her ex-husband, Timothy Affleck, before they divorced in 1984.

Both Ben and Casey credit their parents with instilling in them a love for the arts at a young age, with Casey telling Collider in 2013 that they "started out as children doing this" in part because their "father was in the theater and our mother took us to the theater all the time."

"I got into acting as a young child on account of a sort of arbitrary thing. A friend of my mom’s was a casting director so, really as kind of a lark," Ben told Parade in October 2007. "I had a couple of acting jobs that had just enough exposure to give me the option to continue if I wanted to. I followed through with it."

Ben later had his big break when he won the Academy Award for best original screenplay in 1998, alongside Matt Damon, for their work writing "Good Will Hunting."

CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR THE ENTERTAINMENT NEWSLETTER

Both Ben and Damon brought their mothers with them as their plus-ones for the big ceremony.

"We were sitting next to our moms, and we won, and we kind of hugged our moms. I remember how everyone had made such a big thing out of it as if this was such a novelty," Ben told Vanity Fair in April 2023. "I remember thinking, being insecure, like, ‘Why? Why is it weird that we’re bringing our moms?’ Who else do you think we would bring?"

He continued, "There was nobody else that was going to go. That was it. Of course, our moms were gonna go. That was really innocent and not faked."

LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS

In addition to her two sons, Chris is survived by her five grandchildren: Casey's two children, Indiana and Atticus, and Ben's three children, Violet, Fin and Sam.

item.title: Buttigieg asked about apparent far-left socialist takeover of party as he calls himself a 'Buttigieg Democrat'
item.description: Pete Buttigieg called himself a "common-sense Democrat" but repeatedly avoided disavowing DSA socialism, drawing criticism from Fox News political analyst Reince Priebus.
item.content:encoded:
Former Transportation Secretary and potential 2028 candidate Pete Buttigieg drew criticism from a former RNC chairman when he appeared to sidestep opportunities to disavow the rise of socialism in the Democratic Party and instead called himself a "Buttigieg Democrat."

Speaking on "America Reports" Friday, Buttigieg declined to directly address questions about Democratic Socialists of America (DSA) policies, such as abolishing the Senate and ending deportations, instead criticizing President Donald Trump’s foreign policy and economic record.

"Look, there's always going to be some people in my party who go too far for me, people I disagree with. If you pick the five or 10 or 15 furthest-left people in our party, they're going to, by definition, disagree with a lot of others. But there's so much that we do, in fact, agree on," Buttigieg said.

DEM REP HENRY CUELLAR REJECTS DSA AGENDA, SAYS SOCIALISTS ARE TRYING TO 'USE' DEMOCRATIC PARTY

"I think one of the reasons why you see people who run on a promise of shaking it up, whether it's a DSA candidate on the left or whether it’s someone like Donald Trump, is because people can tell that the system we have is not just showing its age — it's letting us down," he added.

A University of New Hampshire Granite State Poll published Wednesday places Buttigieg neck-and-neck with Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez, D-N.Y., in a potential 2028 match-up. Earlier in July, Ocasio-Cortez responded to concerns about DSA proposals, including abolishing the Senate, calling it a "constitutional question" and noting, "we've all got our complaints."

When pressed on where he falls on the Democratic spectrum, Buttigieg said he doesn’t fit traditional party labels.

KAMALA HARRIS IS THE 'FAIRLY OBVIOUS' 2028 PRESIDENTIAL FRONTRUNNER, DEMOCRATIC INSIDERS SAY

"I'm a Pete Buttigieg Democrat. I think I'm a common-sense Democrat, but of course everybody thinks that their ideas are common sense to them," he said.

Fox News political analyst Reince Priebus, who served as RNC chairman and Trump White House chief of staff, argued on "America Reports" that Buttigieg was refusing to confront the socialist wing of his party, calling the interview an example of mainstream Democrats aligning with "people that are far outside the mainstream."

"The opponent, the Democrats from where Pete Buttigieg is at, is aligning itself with people that are far outside the mainstream. They're on the wrong side of normal, and he didn't really address that when he was pressed," Priebus said. "And that's the big question for him."

MAMDANI-BACKED SOCIALIST WINS IN NEW YORK EXPOSE GROWING RIFT BETWEEN DEMOCRATIC ESTABLISHMENT, INSURGENT LEFT

Priebus’ warnings come after several Democratic socialists won major primary elections, including in New York and Colorado. Melat Kiros, a new candidate backed by the DSA, pulled off an upset in Colorado, defeating longtime Democratic Rep. Diana DeGette in Denver's heavily Democratic district.

In June, a group of far-left candidates won their primary elections in New York with backing from New York City’s Democratic socialist mayor, Zohran Mamdani. The winners included newcomer Darializa Avila Chevalier, who beat Rep. Adriano Espaillat, and Brad Lander, who defeated Rep. Dan Goldman.

Still, when asked whether he was running for president, Buttigieg insisted he was not.

"I'm not running for anything," he said. "I'm helping people who are because this is a very important election where people are seeing that their everyday lives — from the price of gas to healthcare, is on the line — and a lot of people who generally prefer a Republican president still want to see some kind of balance, some kind of check, some kind of restraint, and are considering maybe for the first time in a long time, voting for a Democrat for Congress."

item.title: Joe and Hunter Biden appear on Barstool podcast to present ‘Lib of the Year’ award
item.description: Joe Biden and Hunter Biden surprised Jersey Jerry with a recorded video presenting him the "Lib of the Year" award on "Pardon My Take's" Takie Awards.
item.content:encoded:
Former President Joe Biden and his son Hunter Biden surprised Barstool Sports personality "Jersey Jerry" on Friday in a recorded video, presenting him with the "Lib of the Year" award after he won the title for a third consecutive year during the annual "Pardon My Take" Takie Awards episode.

Jerry appeared stunned after Hunter Biden's video panned to include the former president.

"What the f---? I was not expecting that," Jerry said.

Hunter Biden opened the video by referring to their experience with recovery before congratulating Jerry on his third consecutive victory.

HUNTER BIDEN CALLS MERRICK GARLAND THE 'GREATEST MISTAKE' MADE UNDER THE BIDEN ADMINISTRATION

"Hey, Jerry, from one brother in recovery to another, congratulations on the Lib of the Year award. I know you didn’t have much competition, but I’m still proud of you," Hunter Biden said as the former president appeared beside his son.

"We were both proud of you. Hey, Jerry, congratulations. Keep the faith, Jerry. Congratulations, dude," Joe Biden said.

Jerry struggled to process the cameo as the hosts emphasized that a former president had participated in the comedy sports show's award presentation.

BILL CLINTON CRASHES JERRY JONES' COWBOYS PREDRAFT PRESS CONFERENCE IN SURPRISE APPEARANCE

"Serious? What are we doing?" Jerry said. The hosts replayed the video at Jerry’s request.

"It’s starting to hit me now. Let it hit me for a second," Jerry said.

Jerry jokingly thanked the former president using one of President Donald Trump's longtime nicknames for Joe Biden.

"All right, Sleepy Joe. Thank you, brother," Jerry said.

WATCH: WOULD-BE SECOND-TERM PRESIDENT BIDEN LEFT SEARCHING FOR FAMILY ON STAGE AFTER OBAMA CENTER OPENING

"Pardon My Take" co-host Dan "Big Cat" Katz put the presentation in presidential context.

"Forty-five men have served in 47 presidencies. You have one of 45 men who served as president of the United States of America giving you a Takey for Lib of the Year. Just let that set in for a second. That’s history," Katz said.

Jerry agreed with Katz.

"That is history right there. It’s incredible," he said. "The president knows who I am."

The Biden cameo drew reactions online. Barstool founder Dave Portnoy claimed to be shocked and offered a brief response.

"I gasped," Portnoy said.

DAVE PORTNOY BLASTS USA TODAY COLUMNIST FOR CLAIMING CAITLIN CLARK'S REFEREE COMPLAINTS FUEL RACISM

CLICK HERE FOR MORE COVERAGE OF MEDIA AND CULTURE

Katz celebrated Jerry’s repeated wins.

"Jersey Jerry is going on a dynastic run for Lib of the Year," Katz said.

Barstool media and culture personality "Jack Mac" said the second Biden's appearance also caught him off guard.

"I gasped when the second special guest popped on screen," Jack Mac said.

Former NFL offensive lineman Geoff Schwartz also reacted to the ending, celebrating the parody.

"This is great. Did not expect the end of the video," Schwartz said.

The two-hour, 48-minute episode featured more than 28 awards, including "Take of the Year" and "Blake of the Year." The Takies are the podcast’s annual parody awards.

The segment followed a similar presentation in 2025, where former Transportation Secretary Pete Buttigieg awarded Jerry his second straight title and encouraged him to achieve a three-peat. Buttigieg praised Jerry for his "evolving perspective on immigration" and being "open to the idea that vaccines actually work."

item.title: DHS accuses 'rogue' Clinton judge of open defiance of Supreme Court
item.description: DHS counsel calls the ruling "open defiance of the Supreme Court" after Judge Patti Saris preserves TPS protections for South Sudanese nationals.
item.content:encoded:
The Trump administration is hammering a federal judge for temporarily blocking its effort to end Temporary Protected Status (TPS) for South Sudan despite a recent Supreme Court decision that significantly narrowed lower courts' authority to intervene.

U.S. District Judge Patti Saris on Thursday granted an administrative stay in African Communities Together v. Mullin , preserving TPS protections for South Sudanese nationals while she considers whether plaintiffs may amend their lawsuit and seek renewed relief on constitutional grounds.

The order temporarily freezes the administration's Nov. 6, 2025, decision ending South Sudan's TPS designation, keeping it "null, void, and of no legal effect" until jurisdiction returns to the 1st Circuit. Saris stressed that the order is a procedural measure to preserve the status quo while the court considers the plaintiffs' latest filings and is not a ruling on the merits.

"Another rogue district judge just postponed the termination of TPS for South Sudan," DHS general counsel James Percival wrote on X, slamming the decision. "This is open defiance of the Supreme Court, plain and simple!"

SUPREME COURT WEIGHS TRUMP EFFORT TO TERMINATE TEMPORARY PROTECTIONS FOR HAITIAN, SYRIAN MIGRANTS

Hans von Spakovsky, a senior legal fellow at Advancing American Freedom, echoed that criticism, arguing Saris lacked authority to issue any relief after the Supreme Court's recent TPS ruling.

"She has no right to 'maintain the status quo,'" von Spakovsky told Fox News Digital. "No jurisdiction means no jurisdiction and under the applicable law, the only proper course of judicial action is to dismiss the lawsuits, explaining that based on the law and the Supreme Court's decision, she has no jurisdiction to entertain any claims in her courtroom."

He said the Supreme Court's June decision in Mullin v. Doe reaffirmed that federal law largely bars courts from reviewing or blocking the government's decisions to end Temporary Protected Status.

Although Mullin involved TPS terminations for Syrian and Haitian nationals, von Spakovsky said the Supreme Court's interpretation of the TPS statute applies equally to South Sudan.

SUPREME COURT'S LATEST IMMIGRATION RULING WILL CAUSE AMERICANS TO 'DIE AND SUFFER' ATTORNEY WARNS

"These decisions on Sudanese nationals need to be overturned by the Supreme Court in emergency appeals and the judges need to be disciplined for their misconduct in refusing to follow the Supreme Court decision and the federal law that bans them from questioning decisions made by the executive branch on TPS status," he said.

The criticism stems from the Supreme Court's June 25 decision in Mullin v. Doe, in which a 6-3 majority held that the TPS statute bars courts from reviewing Administrative Procedure Act (APA) challenges to decisions designating or terminating Temporary Protected Status.

The ruling allowed constitutional Equal Protection claims to continue but blocked the APA claims that Saris had relied on in February to delay South Sudan's TPS termination.

"The Supreme Court ruled that district courts lack jurisdiction to review terminations of temporary protected status. I'm confused why some district courts have not yet removed any remaining road blocks," Eric Wessan, Iowa's solicitor general, told Fox News Digital.

Following the Supreme Court's decision, the Justice Department asked the 1st Circuit to reverse Saris' February ruling. The plaintiffs did not oppose the request, instead asking the appeals court to return the case to the district court so they could amend their complaint and pursue only the constitutional claims the Supreme Court left intact. They then asked Saris to temporarily preserve South Sudan's TPS protections while those claims moved forward, a request she granted Thursday.

BLUE STATE LEADERS ERUPT AFTER SUPREME COURT’S DECISION ENDING TPS PROTECTIONS FOR HAITIANS, SYRIANS

The lawsuit was filed in December 2025 by African Communities Together and four South Sudanese immigrants protected by TPS. They allege the Department of Homeland Security unlawfully ended South Sudan's TPS designation without following required procedures and that the decision was motivated by unconstitutional discrimination.

Before the Supreme Court weighed in, Saris repeatedly ruled in favor of the plaintiffs. She first temporarily blocked the TPS termination in December 2025 before issuing a broader postponement in February, finding the plaintiffs were likely to succeed because DHS allegedly failed to follow required procedures, had already decided to end the designation, and offered what the court described as pretextual reasons for doing so.

The Trump administration appealed to the 1st Circuit in March, but Saris declined to stay her own order while the appeal proceeded. The case was later paused pending the Supreme Court's resolution of related TPS disputes involving Haiti and Syria.

SIGN UP TO GET THE POLITICS NEWSLETTER

Saris, who was nominated to the U.S. District Court for the District of Massachusetts by President Bill Clinton in 1993, has presided over a number of high-profile immigration disputes involving both the Trump and Biden administrations.

The temporary order keeps South Sudan's TPS protections in place for now, but the 1st Circuit and potentially the Supreme Court could soon weigh in on whether the district court has the power to do so after the justices' recent TPS decision.

Fox News Digital reached out to the White House and to plaintiffs African Communities Together for comment.

item.title: Caitlin Clark deserves an apology after false USA Today report about getting her hair done
item.description: USA Today falsely reported Caitlin Clark skipped the WNBA Orange Carpet to get her hair done, then issued what it called a mere clarification.
item.content:encoded:
Days after USA Today "reporter" Nancy Armour compared Caitlin Clark allegedly flopping on the basketball court to the people who lynched Black people — no, this isn't satire — the outlet published a false report about why Clark skipped the WNBA Orange Carpet on Thursday.

According to another USA Today "reporter," Heather Burns, Clark skipped the event to "get her hair done in her hometown of Des Moines."

As expected, the report riled up the anti-Clark and anti-White brigades across the WNBA community. How dare she skip the event for a hair appointment?

NANCY ARMOUR'S DISASTROUS CAITLIN CLARK ARTICLE EXEMPLIFIES WHY SPORTSWRITING AND SPORTS MEDIA IS FAILING

Well, she didn't.

Clark missed the event because she was — wait for it — hosting a charity dinner in her hometown.

USA Today finally corrected its false report on Friday, issuing the following note:

"Clarification: Caitlin Clark was attending an event for the Caitlin Clark Foundation, which is why she missed the WNBA All-Star Weekend Orange Carpet."

USA TODAY REPORTER APOLOGIZES FOR INVOKING EMMETT TILL IN COLUMN ABOUT CAITLIN CLARK AFTER UPSETTING THE WOKE

There is, of course, a problem with that "clarification." It wasn't a clarification. It was a full correction. The entire premise of the original report was false.

Further, the outlet owes Clark an apology for publishing inaccurate information that portrayed her in a negative light. USA Today framed Clark as selfish. In reality, her reason for missing the Orange Carpet was anything but selfish.

OutKick contacted USA Today for comment, asking whether it plans to apologize to Clark and whether it will acknowledge that it issued a full correction rather than a mere clarification. The outlet had not responded by the time of publication.

We will update this story if we hear back.

That said, it's difficult to see how USA Today can defend its coverage of Caitlin Clark over the past week. Invoking Emmett Till and lynching in a column about an alleged flop during a basketball game was egregious. The fact that Nancy Armour remains employed undermines whatever credibility the USA Today newsroom has left.

Burns' report was equally troubling. It was so easily disproven that it raises questions about how much effort went into verifying the information before publication. We suspect not much.

Armour and Burns are pathetic journalists. USA Today is a putrid outlet.

"As I tweeted earlier, USA Today is like a hotel chain that kept getting traded to new private equity firms, who wring the money out as it continues to deteriorate," sports media reporter Ryan Glasspiegel told OutKick. "This analogy is ironic in the sense that hotels were a big part of the newspaper's business for several decades."

It might be time for USA Today to shut it down — after it apologizes to Caitlin Clark, of course.

item.title: NYC 'Allahu Akbar' stabbings suspect's charges revealed, yells bizarre message during perp walk
item.description: Raul Morales faces attempted murder and hate crime charges after police said he stabbed two men during separate attacks on Manhattan's Upper West Side
item.content:encoded:
The man accused of stabbing two people while allegedly yelling "Allahu Akbar" on Manhattan's Upper West Side Thursday afternoon has been charged with attempted murder, including hate crime counts tied to one of the victims, according to the New York City Police Department (NYPD).

During a perp walk Friday afternoon, Raul Morales, 51, could be heard yelling "Justice for the Romero family" to reporters, mentioning an unknown woman by name, and vowing, "you're going to remember her name forever." 

It is unclear who the woman is, and what the possible significance is of the remarks.

According to the NYPD, Morales was being transported to Downtown Manhattan for central booking following the perp walk.

WITNESSES RECOUNT 'SCARY' NYC STABBING AFTER SUSPECT ALLEGEDLY YELLED 'ALLAHU AKBAR' DURING ATTACKS

Morales faces attempted murder, assault and criminal possession of a weapon in connection with the stabbing of a 57-year-old Asian man, the NYPD confirmed.

In the attack on a 50-year-old Jewish man, Morales has been charged with attempted murder as a hate crime, assault as a hate crime, assault and criminal possession of a weapon.

Police said the stabbings appeared to be separate attacks that happened near each other Thursday afternoon on the Upper West Side. 

SUSPECT ARRESTED AFTER ALLEGEDLY YELLING ‘ALLAHU AKBAR,' STABBING 2 MEN IN NYC ATTACK

Authorities said there was no known connection between Morales and either victim or between the two victims.

According to police, Morales allegedly yelled "Allahu Akbar" during the attacks. The NYPD is investigating whether bias played a role. 

One victim is Jewish, while the other is Asian, police said.

Both victims were taken to a hospital in stable condition. 

Police said initial findings suggest mental health may have been a factor in the attacks, though Morales had no known mental health history with the NYPD.

New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani condemned the attacks as "hateful and despicable," while New York Gov. Kathy Hochul said she was "disgusted" by what appeared to be another attack targeting the Jewish community.

This is a developing story. Please check back for updates.

item.title: Battleground Dem governor torched for ‘drunken sailor’ spending GOP critic says is symbolic of bigger problem
item.description: Katie Hobbs' reelection campaign burned through $7.4 million in Q2 while raising just $2.64 million, leading to criticism about where support for her campaign is really coming from.
item.content:encoded:
Arizona Democratic Gov. Katie Hobbs’ reelection campaign spent nearly three times what it raised in the second quarter of 2026, burning through more than $7.4 million in three months as a prominent GOP activist in Arizona accused the battleground incumbent of "spending like a drunken sailor" to prop up a struggling campaign.

Campaign finance records reviewed by Fox News Digital show Hobbs’ campaign began the Federal Election Commission's (FEC) Q2 filing period with roughly $7.18 million cash on hand, raised about $2.64 million, spent more than $7.44 million and ended the quarter with about $2.38 million in the bank. The filing shows much of the spending went toward communications, TV, advertising and outside campaign firms, giving Republicans a fresh line of attack as Hobbs seeks reelection in one of the nation’s most closely watched battleground gubernatorial races.

"She’s spending like a drunken sailor. And drunken sailors typically don’t spend smart," Turning Point USA chief operating officer, former Maricopa County GOP chair and 7th generation Arizonan Tyler Bowyer told Fox News Digital. "When you’re spending that much money on consultants and TV and paid messaging, that tells me there isn’t a lot of organic energy behind the campaign."

TOP DEMOCRAT GOVERNORS ARE HOPING TO RIDE THEIR RECORDS TO THE WHITE HOUSE. CAN THEY?

Bowyer said the filing reflects a broader challenge for Democrats in Arizona, and nationally, saying Hobbs’ campaign spending more than it raised is "a huge problem" for an incumbent Democrat in a battleground state.

Among those problems, Bowyer argued, is a spending strategy focused heavily on paid media and consultants rather than grassroots energy. He pointed to what he described as "a whole lot" of spending on consultants, TV and paid messaging, noting, "these are not real grassrootsy types of moves," and arguing that campaigns with less organic support often struggle down the stretch.

Hobbs, who narrowly won the governor’s office in 2022 against then-Republican challenger Kari Lake, is seeking reelection in a state expected to be one of the most closely watched political battlegrounds of the 2026 cycle. 

She won her uncontested primary Tuesday and will advance to the general election to take on Trump-backed Republican nominee Rep. Andy Biggs, R-Ariz., who beat out several opponents to win his Tuesday primary. Biggs’ campaign also seized on Hobbs' spending earlier this month, accusing the incumbent governor of "lighting" $7.4 million "on fire" and highlighting what it described as a 281% Q2 burn rate.

TRUMP FLEXES GOP MUSCLE IN ARIZONA PRIMARIES AS DEMS DODGE FAR-LEFT UPSET

"While Andy Biggs’ campaign is floundering and stuck defending his decision to side with a pedophile cult over protecting women and children, we’re proud of the strong support we’ve received from grassroots donors in all 15 Arizona counties," Hobbs campaign manager, Nicole DeMont, told Fox News Digital in response to the criticism about the governor's spending numbers.

The "pedophile cult" reference appeared to point to a recent Hobbs campaign digital ad that accused Biggs of "protecting predators," citing his opposition to a bill addressing Arizona’s rape-kit backlog and his vote against releasing the Epstein files.

"We’re going to continue using those resources to reach Arizonans across the state in both English and Spanish through face-to-face conversations, community organizing, and on their TVs, local radio stations, and digital platforms."

But, aside from whether Hobbs is earning grassroots support, Bowyer also cast Hobbs’ burn rate as part of a broader problem for the Democratic Party, arguing that the party is spending aggressively to keep pace with Republicans heading into the midterms even though Democrats are the party out of power in Washington and would typically expect the president’s party to face tougher headwinds.

He added that Hobbs’ cash position matters beyond her own campaign because Arizona does not have a Senate race this cycle to help drive Democratic fundraising and turnout infrastructure.

"If the governor doesn't have money, then a lot of candidates down ballot won't have a ton of money," he said, arguing Democrats often rely on federal races as a "crutch" to support campaigns lower on the ticket.

Meanwhile, Bowyer said the race should also matter to conservatives outside Arizona because the state is expected to remain central to the 2028 presidential map. He argued that Republicans need to invest now in battleground states like Arizona to build the organization, funding and "boots on the ground" needed for the next White House race.

"Right now, we’re in the battle of our lives for what 2030 and beyond will look like," Bowyer said. "People are totally underestimating what this country will look like if the Democrats win the presidency in 2028 and hijack the census process and redistricting."

"We may look back at 2026 and realize that was the pivot point where we saved America ahead of 2028, or we lost America for good."

item.title: ICC prosecutor whose Netanyahu warrant fueled Mamdani arrest threat is fired over sexual misconduct
item.description: ICC member states voted to remove chief prosecutor Karim Khan over sexual misconduct allegations, marking the first such dismissal in the court's history. His lawyer says he will appeal decision.
item.content:encoded:
The International Criminal Court prosecutor whose arrest warrant against Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu became central to New York Mayor Zohran Mamdani’s threat to arrest the Israeli leader was dismissed Friday after member states voted to remove him over sexual misconduct allegations.

Karim Khan, the ICC’s chief prosecutor, was removed after a vote by the Assembly of States Parties, the court’s 125-member governing body, following disciplinary proceedings tied to allegations involving a junior female staffer in his office. Khan has denied wrongdoing.

The decision marked the first time in the ICC’s history that a sitting chief prosecutor has been removed from office. Khan’s removal comes days after Secretary of State Marco Rubio launched a U.S. campaign to "dismantle" the ICC, accusing the court of threatening American sovereignty.

MAMDANI GOES BACK ON CAMPAIGN PROMISE, SAYS NYC CAN'T ARREST NETANYAHU

Khan became one of the world’s most controversial prosecutors after pursuing ICC arrest warrants for Netanyahu and former Israeli Defense Minister Yoav Gallant over Israel’s war against Hamas in Gaza. The ICC issued the warrants in November 2024, prompting fierce condemnation from Israel and the United States, neither of which is a member of the court.

The warrants also became a flashpoint in New York politics after Mamdani repeatedly invoked the ICC case against Netanyahu. Mamdani said during his campaign that he would seek to arrest Netanyahu if the Israeli prime minister came to New York, and later acknowledged as mayor that the city lacks authority to enforce the warrant while calling on the federal government to do so.

The ICC, based in The Hague in Holland, is a permanent international court created under the Rome Statute to prosecute individuals accused of genocide, war crimes, crimes against humanity and the crime of aggression when national courts are unable or unwilling to act.

WORLD COURT PROSECUTOR WHO WENT AFTER NETANYAHU FOR WAR CRIMES SUSPENDED OVER SEXUAL MISCONDUCT

The allegations against Khan have triggered a crisis for the court. Reuters reported that 82 of the ICC’s 125 member states voted in favor of his removal, exceeding the absolute majority required. Khan had previously stepped aside in May 2025 while a U.N. oversight investigation was underway and was suspended in June 2026 pending the final vote.

The Associated Press reported that the court’s oversight body found Khan had committed "serious misconduct." The case involved allegations from a female aide who said Khan engaged in nonconsensual sexual conduct. Khan’s lawyers have denied the allegations and called the removal process legally flawed and unsupported by evidence.

The woman, identified only as Sarah, went public in a CNN interview last week. "There is no way for something to be consensual when you have such a power disparity," she told CNN.

Khan’s legal team rejected the vote and said he would challenge the decision. Tayab Ali, partner at Bindmans LLP and head of Khan’s legal team, said in a statement that the Assembly of States Parties had disregarded due process concerns raised publicly by more than 180 nongovernmental organizations and senior international lawyers.

"The decision is unsupported by any lawful or properly reasoned finding that Mr Khan KC committed misconduct or breached his duties as Prosecutor," Ali said. "He has denied the allegations from the outset and continues to do so." Ali said the allegations were investigated for more than a year by the U.N. Office of Internal Oversight Services and argued that "there is not a single finding of misconduct, including sexual misconduct, anywhere in the OIOS report." He also said a three-judge panel unanimously determined in March 2026 that the factual findings made by OIOS did not establish misconduct or breach of duty by Khan.


Khan’s lawyers accused the Assembly of States Parties of removing him through a politically driven and procedurally unfair process, saying Khan and his lawyers were not allowed to make formal submissions to the Assembly before the vote.

"The Prosecutor of this Court has been removed by an executive vote while under sanctions and while the Court is under immense political pressure," Ali said.
Ali said Khan "will challenge the lawfulness and fairness of the decision through all available legal mechanisms."

Israeli officials argued Friday that Khan’s removal undermined the legitimacy of the ICC’s actions against Netanyahu.

Israeli Ambassador to the United Nations Danny Danon told Fox News Digital that Khan believed "by launching a political witch hunt against Israel and issuing a politically-motivated arrest warrant against Prime Minister Netanyahu, the world would ignore the grave sexual misconduct allegations against him."

"He was wrong," Danon said. "He sought to scapegoat Israel in an attempt to divert attention from his own misconduct. The international community rejected that cynical attempt today."

NETANYAHU FIRES BACK AT NYC MAYOR MAMDANI'S VOW TO ENFORCE 'BOGUS ARREST WARRANT'

Danon added, "The attacks against Israel, which were intended to distract from his disgraceful conduct, did not save Karim Khan, and they will not help Zohran Mamdani either."

Anne Bayefsky, president of Human Rights Voices and director of the Touro Institute on Human Rights and the Holocaust, told Fox News Digital that Khan’s fall should not be viewed as an isolated scandal. "He unexpectedly requested arrest warrants for Israel’s prime minister and defense minister within weeks of discovering his sexual deviancy had been revealed. He accused his victim of being a Mossad agent. He and his lawyers constantly repeated the refrain that Israelis were behind the accusations."

Bayefsky claimed that Khan’s conduct has damaged the ICC itself. "Now there is a massive campaign to save the ICC from Khan. On this logic, Khan’s anti-Israel fanaticism never tainted his investigation of Israel, his arrest warrant request against Israelis, his submissions to the ICC Court, the evidence he placed before the Court, or the analysis and conclusions of the ICC Court that placed their trust in him when they decided to grant his warrant requests."

The ICC has not said Khan’s removal affects the Netanyahu and Gallant warrants, which were issued by judges after Khan’s request.

Requests sent to Khan's office for comment were not answered by the time of publication.

item.title: James Carville blasts far-left 'White turds' among Dems who he says value Lenin more than MLK
item.description: James Carville warned democratic socialists value communist leader Vladimir Lenin over Martin Luther King Jr. and calls far-left politicians paternalistic on his podcast.
item.content:encoded:
Veteran Democratic strategist James Carville condemned far-left Democrats on Thursday, warning that they value Soviet dictators more than American civil rights leaders.

Carville has spent years warning the Democratic Party to distance itself from far-left culture-war politics. In recent months, with the rise of democratic socialists, however, Carville has gone so far as to suggest the party should have a schism to keep radicals from taking power.

On Thursday, he also recalled other socialist politicians taking far-left positions ranging from calls to indict Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu to speaking out against interracial dating.

"Let me tell you something," Carville began, offering a warning to Black voters and to other more centrist liberals like himself, "They think they know more than you do. "Someday James is going to tell us what he really thinks," his co-host Al Hunt joked.

"You can see this coming," Carville continued, warning, "It's always been ... they’ve got to be part of the movement. The only movement they got is a f---ing bowel movement."

item.title: Alveda King slams USA Today columnist for invoking Emmett Till in Caitlin Clark piece: 'Pure race-baiting'

"What people have learned to do, is to throw out inflammatory, emotional phrases that will make people emotional and forget how to think. There was no reason to throw Emmett Till's name out there. And so, that's called race-baiting," she continued.

King's advice to Americans is simple: Don't be "misled by emotional turmoil without examining the facts."

What are the facts here?

NANCY ARMOUR'S DISASTROUS CAITLIN CLARK ARTICLE EXEMPLIFIES WHY SPORTSWRITING AND SPORTS MEDIA IS FAILING

Surely, Nancy has reached out to civil rights pundits and race historians, right?

OutKick reached out to the NAACP national office for this story on Thursday to add its own perspective. We have not heard back.

item.title: Mike Vrabel untouched by Dianna Russini scandal at first press conference of Patriots training camp
item.description: Mike Vrabel faced zero questions about the Dianna Russini scandal as Patriots players reported for training camp, signaling he may have moved past it.
item.content:encoded:
The drama that shadowed coach Mike Vrabel during the offseason due to his relationship with NFL reporter Dianna Russini was nowhere to be seen Friday when New England Patriots players reported for training camp.

Vrabel must feel he's not only survived but surmounted the ongoing nature of the saga because, well, the thing is not a public topic now as his team gets ready for its first practice on Saturday.

PATRIOTS COACH MIKE VRABEL BREAKS SILENCE ON DIANNA RUSSINI PHOTOS THAT LED TO 'DIFFICULT CONVERSATIONS'

Vrabel, in his second year as the Patriots coach, met with reporters for more than 14 minutes on Friday to kick off the start of camp.

And he fielded not one question about the Russini scandal or anything connected to it.

It was all football – which Vrabel deftly handles like Ted Williams did fastballs back in the day.

Vrabel was asked about the status of second-round draft pick Gabe Jacas, who remains unsigned. Reporters indeed concentrated six of their 20 or so questions to Vrabel on the Jacas topic.

How's the contract negotiations?

How's his health?

Football stuff.

But, again, nothing about the coach and the overriding issue he faced starting April 7 when the New York Post published photographs of him and Russini, then working for The Athletic, enjoying private time at a pool, and in a hot tub, and holding hands and embracing at an Arizona resort before the NFL annual meeting.

Those photos kicked off consistent national coverage that sometimes bordered on cringey – including other photos of the pair at a bar or other events while their spouses were not present. They also predictably led to something of a crisis within the Vrabel family.

Vrabel, in fact, removed himself from the final day of the NFL draft so that he could be with his family and said he was taking time to seek counseling.

But on Friday, nobody asked if the counseling sessions are over or continue.

One would think that if a Super Bowl contender's coach is in counseling, which he made public, someone might wonder if the sessions continue during a hectic training camp.

Or possibly bleed into the season.

Somebody might want to know if Vrabel thinks the counseling succeeded. Or failed. Like, what has changed for Vrabel as a result of those sessions he so publicly announced he was about to undergo?

There was no question to Vrabel at the podium about any of that or anything else having to do with the Russini saga.

We already know Vrabel isn't going to be fired, or even disciplined, for being part of the embarrassment and unwanted attention he brought on himself, the Patriots, and the NFL as a result of this story.

But Friday's presser sealed the fact Vrabel has successfully avoided a major distraction to start training camp.

That actually is his first victory of the season.

Russini, meanwhile, has clearly lost. She resigned from her job at The Athletic and the media company has apparently replaced her with a new so-called insider. She remains at the heart of an internal investigation by the New York Times, which owns The Athletic, with the results of that not yet published.

So barring more facts coming to light, such as the publication of the investigation, Vrabel skates. If he didn't get asked about his counseling sessions and family status on Friday, the chances that happens going forward shrink daily.

So, yes, Vrabel is 1-0 already to kick off training camp.

As one of OutKick's resident Florida fans — along with Austin Perry — Nick is right, by the way. There won't be a ton of patience for Jon Sumrall. Believe me. The Gators have STUNK for years now, and it's been unacceptable.

item.title: CNN host admits he was wrong to say illegal immigrant voting 'never happens' after New Jersey error
item.description: Michael Smerconish says he can no longer claim noncitizen voting never happens after New Jersey revealed a software error registered 6,600 noncitizens.
item.content:encoded:
CNN and SiriusXM host Michael Smerconish acknowledged Wednesday on "The Michael Smerconish Program" that he could no longer claim noncitizen voting never occurred after New Jersey disclosed that a software error improperly registered roughly 6,600 noncitizens and fewer than 400 cast ballots.

"I can’t say that any longer," Smerconish said. "I don’t know how often it does happen, but I can’t say any longer, ‘This never happens.’"

Smerconish said he had previously reached the opposite conclusion after discussing a January New York Times analysis titled "Initial Review Finds No Widespread Illegal Voting by Migrants, Puncturing a Trump Claim." The analysis found no evidence of widespread fraud but noted that noncitizens sometimes appeared on voter rolls.

Smerconish said the New Jersey disclosure would give President Donald Trump and his allies a lasting response when opponents disputed that noncitizen voting occurred.

GOP ERUPTS OVER 6,600 NONCITIZEN VOTERS FOUND IN BLUE STATE AS SCANDAL DEEPENS: ‘WORSE THAN ANYONE EXPECTED’

"'Well, what about New Jersey?' See, it actually does happen," Smerconish said, in a clip flagged by Mediaite.

Political analyst Mark Halperin agreed that the disclosure undercut categorical claims about noncitizen voting while cautioning that more information was needed before conclusions could be reached about its scale.

"Based on what we now know, the thing that Democrats said doesn’t happen happened," Halperin said. "And it’s not right to take the word of the Democratic governor of New Jersey about what actually happened."

Halperin called for an independent investigation into how the registrations occurred, whether the same problem appeared elsewhere and whether New Jersey’s estimate captured the full extent of the error.

WATCH: TRUMP DOJ VOWS TO PURSUE ‘EVERY SINGLE’ VOTING VIOLATION AFTER NJ ROLL SHOCKER

"If it happened by accident on this small scale, it requires a lot more explanation and investigation about whether it’s happened in New Jersey more or elsewhere," Halperin said. "But the scale is not very significant. So we need to know more."

Fox News Digital reached out to New Jersey Gov. Mike Sherrill for comment, but did not immediately receive a response.

Sherrill said the error affected people who indicated they were not U.S. citizens while applying for driver's licenses or identification cards between June 2023 and June 2024. The system nevertheless registered them to vote.

"Our preliminary analysis shows fewer than 400 individuals who were newly registered for the first time because of the error voted," Sherrill said. "They were registered as Democrats, Republicans and Unaffiliated voters and were scattered across the state."

NEW JERSEY REMOVES 6,600 PEOPLE FROM VOTER ROLLS WHO WERE ELIGIBLE TO CAST A BALLOT FOR 2024 ELECTION

Sherrill ordered the affected registrations removed, launched an investigation and began replacing IDEMIA, the vendor involved with the Motor Vehicle Commission system. She blamed failures under former Democratic Gov. Phil Murphy's administration.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE COVERAGE OF MEDIA AND CULTURE

"This failure didn’t occur under my watch, but accountability starts now," Sherrill said.

IDEMIA disputed efforts to place responsibility solely on the company, telling Fox News Digital that New Jersey election officials were responsible for determining eligibility.

"The voter registration information is transmitted to the New Jersey Department of State, Division of Elections, which is ultimately responsible for verifying eligibility to vote," IDEMIA said.

The Justice Department subsequently demanded information about the 6,600 registrations and the fewer than 400 people who voted. Assistant Attorney General Harmeet Dhillon gave the state five days to provide names, registration details and voting records.

"Ensuring that U.S. citizens’ votes are not illegally diluted by noncitizens’ votes is of paramount importance," Dhillon said.

item.title: Republicans target Trump's crypto empire with new plan, Dems say it falls short
item.description: Trump's income surged 250% to $2.2 billion largely from crypto ventures, but Senate Democrats say the Clarity Act's ethics provisions fall short.
item.content:encoded:
Senate Republicans want to rein in President Donald Trump’s income explosion since returning to the White House, but Democrats aren’t sold on how they’re going to do it.

The Senate is on the cusp of moving landmark cryptocurrency legislation known as the Clarity Act that, if passed, proponents say would finally fold the novel currency into the nation’s web of financial regulations.

Tucked away in the over 600-page package are a slate of ethics provisions that target Trump, the vice president and their spouses. The White House signed off on the provisions, and the architects of the bill say that the restrictions reach beyond just Trump and target lawmakers, too.

GOP RIFT GROWS AS THUNE HITS BRAKES ON TRUMP'S ELECTION BILL TO AVERT SHUTDOWN

But for now, it’s not enough for Senate Democrats.

"Someone can call it an ethics provision," Sen. Elizabeth Warren, D-Mass., said. "But if it doesn't stop the president from profiting off of crypto, and using it as a way to take bribes right out in public. Then it's not really any expedition.

The list of guardrails included preventing federal officials from creating their own digital currency for profit, promoting or endorsing crypto, creating a divestiture or blind trust requirement one year after enactment, allowing officials to own crypto and a disclosure of crypto sales.

Sen. Cynthia Lummis, R-Wyo., who has led the effort on the Clarity Act, told Fox News’ Maria Bartiromo that the idea isn’t to "plan legislation around one person who holds one office for the next two years, but rather, over time, that will serve the House, the Senate, the judiciary, and the executive branch in a fair way."

HOUSE GOP VOTES TO PUNT GOVERNMENT SHUTDOWN BATTLE TO AFTER NOVEMBER MIDTERMS

"The struggle is, of course, a lot of Democrats are absolutely focused on one person, and that's President Trump," Lummis said. "So since President Trump actually agreed that he would have the choice to either put his assets in a blind trust, or divest of his participation in digital assets and companies that derive revenue from digital assets, somehow, that's not enough."

There are other gripes with the package, but the ethics provisions are proving a sharp red line. That’s because Trump’s income between 2024 and 2025 erupted by about 250% — from just over $620 million to about $2.2 billion.

And much of that increase is attributed to his various holdings and ventures in crypto, which are run by his sons, Don Jr. and Eric, according to the president’s financial disclosure forms reviewed by Fox News Digital.

Trump’s income shot up by $1.4 billion during his first year in office thanks to earnings from the $TRUMP memecoin, World Liberty Financial token sales and Stablecoin Holdco, among others.

Sen. Bernie Moreno, R-Ohio, who alongside Sen. Cynthia Lummis, R-Wyo., worked with the White House to draft the ethics provisions, said that the "behavior" that was being targeted was issuance, promotion, and sponsorship of crypto.

"Again, a very different standard than Nancy Pelosi was held to," Moreno said.

REPUBLICAN SAYS TRUMP'S TOP ELECTION PRIORITY 'DEAD' IN SENATE AS GOP FRACTURES AHEAD OF MIDTERMS

When asked about Democrats already raising issues with the provisions, Moreno told Fox News Digital, "They're always obsessed with putting things into the base bill, just offer an amendment."

"That’s the way this place was built, you know, let's put the base bill out there," he said. "The ethics piece is this much of the bill — Tiny bit — just offer an amendment."

Democrats have noted that the ethics provisions don’t specifically target his sons, meaning that the Trump family crypto empire, which has heavily benefited from his name and time in office, would be left largely unchecked.

They also put sole enforcement power into the hands of Acting Attorney General Todd Blanche, a close ally of Trump’s, and are set to sunset on Jan. 20, 2029, when Trump will have left office.

Sen. Cory Booker, D-N.J., told Fox News Digital that he still has "a lot of ethics concerns, and there’s still work to do."

"This is the partisan draft. It's very obviously not going anywhere," Booker said. "If there's only one pathway to do this it’s doing (it in) a bipartisan manner. There are enough of us on both sides of the aisle that we should be able to land this. It's good faith negotiations."

The objections to the bill, for now, appear to be slowing its roll through the Senate as the upper chamber sprints to a monthlong break in August, and deals with a shrinking window of opportunity to finish legislation before the year is out.

Senate Majority Leader John Thune, R-S.D., had hoped to get the Clarity Act on the floor next week, but acknowledged that might not be possible.

"I don’t think we’ll be able to get it done, but I would like to at least get Clarity started," he said.

item.title: DNC panel picks first 2028 primary state after battle over key voting blocs
item.description: The DNC Rules and Bylaws panel voted to keep South Carolina as the first 2028 Democratic primary, choosing it over Nevada in a battle over voter outreach.
item.content:encoded:
South Carolina is on course to remain the lead-off primary in the Democratic Party's 2028 presidential nominating calendar, after landing a key party committee's recommendation.

The Democratic National Committee's (DNC) powerful Rules and Bylaws panel, meeting in the nation's capital on Friday, picked South Carolina over Nevada to hold the party's first presidential nominating contest in 2028, a move that will likely maintain a key role in the primary calendar for Black voters, who are a crucial part of the Democrats' base.

The vote comes after intense lobbying by both states, as well as by New Hampshire, and Iowa over the past year to hold the much-coveted lead-off Democratic primary in the race for the White House. And the battle between South Carolina and Nevada was seen as a struggle between rewarding Black voters, who have long been loyal Democratic voters, and outreach to Latino voters, with whom President Donald Trump and Republicans made major gains in the 2024 election, handing Democrats major setbacks.

The panel also voted to allow Nevada, New Hampshire, Michigan, Virginia, and New Mexico to hold primaries in the early voting window, before the rest of the states hold nominating contests starting ahead of Super Tuesday.

WHO'S UP AND WHO'S DOWN: CHECK OUT THE FOX NEWS POWER RANKINGS ON THE MIDTERM ELECTIONS

According to the panel, South Carolina would hold its primary on Jan. 22, 2028, with Nevada going second on Feb. 1, 2028, followed by New Hampshire on Feb. 8, 2028. New Mexico would hold the fourth contest, on Feb. 15, 2028, followed by Michigan on Feb. 22, 2028, and Virginia on Feb. 29, 2028.

The Rules and Bylaws Committee's proposals on the calendar will face a final vote by the DNC's entire membership when the party holds its summer meeting next month in Austin, Texas.

Minyon Moore, the panel's co-chair, said that South Carolina "will emerge as the first contest."

South Carolina supporters pointed to the recent Supreme Court ruling that weakened the Voting Rights Act, and the ongoing redistricting battles, and argued that the party needs to reaffirm its commitment to Black voters when their electoral strength has been diminished.

Nevada allies, meanwhile, pointed to the western battleground state's diverse electorate of Latino, Black, Asian American and Pacific Islanders, and its working class population as the ideal state for Democratic White House hopefuls to make their case.

New Hampshire held the lead-off presidential primary for both Democrats and Republicans for a century, and while the GOP adhered to tradition in the last race for the White House, the DNC upended its calendar, placing South Carolina ahead of the Granite State. The move was seen as an unwanted distraction for Democrats during the 2024 primaries.

AOC SURGES PAST BUTTIGIEG, LEAVES HARRIS IN THE DUST: NEW POLL IN KEY 2028 PRIMARY STATE

National Democrats for years had knocked both Iowa — whose caucuses for 50 years led off the party’s nominating calendar until 2024 — and New Hampshire as unrepresentative of the party as a whole because the states have largely white populations with few major urban areas. Nevada and South Carolina, which are much more diverse than either Iowa or New Hampshire, were added near the top of the Democratic calendar two decades ago to increase the diversity of the early states’ electorate

.

New Hampshire Democrats have long pushed back, saying the state’s rich tradition of grassroots, retail politics, its well-informed electorate, its high percentage of voter participation and its longtime status as a key general election swing state make it the perfect locale to hold the first-in-the-nation primary.

After the DNC removed New Hampshire from the top of its 2024 calendar, putting the state second along with Nevada, the Granite State still moved to the head of the line. Adhering to a half-century-old law that mandates the Granite State to hold the first presidential primary a week ahead of any similar contest, New Hampshire Secretary of State Dave Scanlan scheduled the Democratic and GOP presidential primary contests for Jan. 23, 2024.

The Democratic contest, which was held before South Carolina and Nevada, ended up being an unsanctioned election, with the DNC banning the state's delegates from attending that summer's nominating convention. The DNC later made peace with New Hampshire and reinstated their convention delegates.

But this time around, the party is proposing much more lethal sanctions against states that go rogue, as well as tough penalties on candidates who campaign in those states, in hopes of preventing unsanctioned contests.

SIGN UP TO GET THE POLITICS NEWSLETTER

"Because of this calendar, our candidates will be tested," said DNC Chair Ken Martin. "Because of this process, millions more Americans will be heard. Because of this committee, our party is and will be stronger. And because of the work that all of us have done together, our eventual nominee will enter the general election, prepared to unite our coalition to compete in every part of the country and to win back the White House."

But longtime New Hampshire Democratic Party Chair Ray Buckley, in a statement after the vote on the calendar, argued, "Today’s vote shows that many party insiders have learned nothing from 2024. New Hampshire has a proven track record of testing our candidates with a rigorous, fair, and efficient process, yet those qualities did not prevail. This committee’s vote does not change the realities governing New Hampshire’s primary, which are beyond the control of both this committee and our state party."

DEMOCRACY ’26: STAY UP TO DATE WITH THE FOX NEWS ELECTION HUB

Nevada Democratic Party Chair Daniele Monroe-Moreno emphasized in a statement, "As an early state and the first true test of a candidate’s ability to win in a general election, we will play a critical role in the nomination process."

While Democrats have argued over their 2028 calendar, the rival Republican National Committee announced earlier this year that their nominating schedule, with Iowa and New Hampshire as the lead-off contests, would be unchanged.

item.title: Spiny lobster mini season kicks off in Florida, drawing eager divers to the water
item.description: Florida's spiny lobster mini season arrives the last Wednesday and Thursday of July, and here's what you need to know about limits and permits.
item.content:encoded:
Summer is in full swing in South Florida, but if you've been down here at any point in the last few months or you own a thermometer, you're probably aware of that.

With the calendar rapidly approaching the last week in July, it's easy to get down about summer coming to an end, but it also means we are closing in on the most wonderful time of the year.

No, I'm not talking about Christmas. It's spiny lobster mini season here in the Sunshine State.

TWO REGULAR JOES WILL COMPETE WITH PROS FOR $3.25M PURSE AT INAUGURAL 'THE CHAMPIONS' BASS FISHING TOURNAMENT

If you're unfamiliar with mini season, it's basically a time where commercial fishers aren't allowed to catch any lobsters so that anyone who does so recreationally can have first dibs.

It happens the last Wednesday and Thursday of July every year, and every hotel along the Florida Keys braces in anticipation for the mass pilgrimage of both natives and visitors who will make the trek down to participate.

For those who wish to partake in the wonders of mini season, there are some rules you must follow.

You are limited to 12 lobsters per person per day, unless you are diving in Monroe County (home of the Florida Keys). If you're staying there, your limit is six per person per day.

Also, keep an eye out for protected areas and National and State Parks, as those are obviously no-take zones.

In addition to the limit, you must also make sure the carapace (the part from its head to the beginning of the tail) exceeds 3 inches in length. You must also have a lobster permit, which you can easily obtain by going to the Florida Fish and Wildlife Conservation Commission's website.

After all that is taken care of, the fun really begins.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE SPORTS COVERAGE ON FOXNEWS.COM

I'm not even a big fan of eating lobster at a restaurant, but I have happily devoured pounds of Florida spiny lobster that my friends and family have caught while staying in The Keys.

Much like with fish, you will never have a more delicious lobster than the one you caught yourself.

One of the beauties of diving for lobster during mini season is that you don't need any fancy gear to have a great time, either.

Sure, it helps to have dive tanks and SCUBA gear, but plenty of spots along the Gulf waters are shallow enough - particularly in the Upper and Middle Keys - that all you need is a mask, snorkel, a pair of gloves, and a kayak to hit your daily limit.

The lobsters love to hide in little holes, crevices, and even underneath old sunken personal items, so be sure to leave no stone unturned (literally).

I would recommend staying the whole week even though the actual season is only from Wednesday through Thursday so that you can partake in the other activity that area is famous for: fishing.

SIGN UP TO GET THE LATEST SPORTS NEWS

When you aren't out diving for lobster, there is plenty of world class fishing to be done all up and down both coasts of the Florida Keys.

As a native Floridian, my summers never feel complete without taking the journey down to our state's most famous archipelago in late July, and I'm hoping some of you are able to experience that magic for yourselves.

Summer is all about creating memories that last a lifetime, and I can't think of a better place to create some new ones than the Florida Keys during spiny lobster mini season.

item.title: 5 options to replace Ryan Clark on ESPN's Super Bowl halftime show
item.description: Kurt Warner, Steve Smith Sr., Dan Orlovsky and Mina Kimes are among five candidates to replace Ryan Clark on ESPN's Super Bowl halftime show.
item.content:encoded:
The biggest-picture takeaway from ESPN's decision to part ways with Ryan Clark is that it opens a seat on the network's coverage of its first-ever Super Bowl this February.

Clark was one of three analysts on "Monday Night Countdown," which is expected to serve as ESPN's official Super Bowl pregame and halftime show. Jason Kelce and Marcus Spears are the other analysts, while Scott Van Pelt is expected to return as host.

From ESPN's perspective, the timing makes sense. The Super Bowl halftime show could draw more than 140 million viewers. The network could not allow Clark to represent the brand during its biggest broadcast ever, given his history of bigoted remarks.

ZERO BS. JUST DAKICH. TAKE THE DON'T @ ME PODCAST ON THE ROAD. DOWNLOAD NOW!

So, here are five possible replacements for ESPN:

Of the internal candidates, Kurt Warner makes the most sense.

As part of ESPN's acquisition of NFL Network assets, the company now has access to Warner. He would give the network a Hall of Fame quarterback on the panel, something that has traditionally been a staple of major NFL studio shows.

Troy Aikman is the only other Hall of Fame quarterback on ESPN's roster, but he'll be in the booth calling the game.

One logistical hurdle remains. Warner currently serves as the lead analyst for Westwood One's "Monday Night Football" radio broadcasts, including the Super Bowl.

Sources tell OutKick ESPN could use Warner on the pregame show because he's already on site each week for the radio broadcast. He would have to step away from his Westwood One duties, however, to serve as ESPN's halftime analyst.

As WFAN host Craig Carton argued this week, Warner would almost certainly choose television over radio, if he's able to get out of his contract. Whether that's possible remains unclear.

Steve Smith Sr. is another analyst ESPN inherited from NFL Network.

Interestingly, Smith could also assume some of Clark's day-to-day responsibilities. Sources say he impressed ESPN decision makers during appearances on "First Take" around the NFL Draft. With the network planning to better separate the guest lineups between "First Take" and "Get Up" this season, Smith could earn a regular role on one or both shows.

That also makes him a logical candidate for "Monday Night Countdown."

Dan Orlovsky is ESPN's best daily NFL analyst and would give the panel a former quarterback.

He's also the opposite of Ryan Clark in one important respect. Few personalities at ESPN are less likely to drift away from football and into unrelated topics than Orlovsky is. Such decision-making is underrated.

Orlovsky has become one of the network's more recognizable NFL voices through "NFL Live," "Get Up," "First Take," and "The Pat McAfee Show."

Scheduling may be the biggest obstacle. Last season, Orlovsky stayed in New York on Mondays for "Get Up" and "First Take" instead of traveling with NFL Live to the Monday Night Football site.

ESPN may decide he's more valuable anchoring its morning lineup, especially after moving on from Cam Newton. Orlovsky and his representatives could just as easily argue for a schedule that allows him to do both, by moving his morning show responsibilities to later in the week.

USA TODAY WRITER SAYS CAITLIN CLARK PUTS BLACK AND QUEER WNBA PLAYERS 'IN DANGER' BY FLOPPING

To be clear, we're not suggesting ESPN should choose Mina Kimes as its Super Bowl halftime analyst. We think that would be a mistake.

However, we'd be surprised if her name isn't, at least, mentioned internally.

Because some critics have predictably accused ESPN of racism for moving on from Clark, it's possible executives feel pressure to make a symbolic personnel move. Kimes would almost certainly be part of that discussion.

Choosing someone who never played or coached in the NFL for ESPN's first Super Bowl halftime show, however, would erase much of the goodwill the network has built with football fans over the past few days.

Another option is simply moving one of ESPN's Sunday pregame shows to Mondays, be it Randy Moss, Alex Smith, Rex Ryan, and Tedy Bruschi.

Each would be an upgrade over Clark, and by a substantial margin. Moss is the biggest star from his playing career. Bruschi is the strongest television analyst of the four.

There's another possibility worth considering.

Networks carrying the Super Bowl often supplement their studio coverage with active players whose seasons have ended during the postseason. Given how much emphasis ESPN is placing on its first Super Bowl, don't be surprised if the network adds a major current or recently retired player alongside its existing crew, even if just for the one broadcast.

Names like Matthew Stafford, Jameis Winston, Kirk Cousins, or Joe Flacco come to mind.

Or, perhaps for a one-time appearance, ESPN could pair Jason Kelce with his brother, Travis Kelce, who is expected to retire at the end of the Chiefs' season.

item.title: New York Times removes ex-Venezuelan Dictator Nicolás Maduro from 'Most Stylish' of 2026 list
item.description: The New York Times quietly removed Nicolás Maduro from its style list after a meme of the captured Venezuelan dictator in an tracksuit went viral.
item.content:encoded:
The New York Times removed ex-Venezuelan dictator Nicolás Maduro from their "39-ish Most Sylish People of 2026" list earlier this month, according to an editor's note.

The note at the bottom of the list, dated July 7, read, "This article has been updated to remove an entry on Nicolás Maduro. Read our Styles story about how an image of him in a tracksuit became a meme."

The outlet's style section reported on how President Donald Trump's Truth Social post of a photo of Maduro in a grey tracksuit following his capture went viral and quickly became a meme.

Page Six first reported the removal on Friday. The list was published by the Times on July 7.

NEW YORK TIMES BLASTS ‘ABUSIVE’ TRUMP SUBPOENAS TARGETING REPORTERS’ SOURCES

The Times' style piece about Maduro from January read, "Despite the seriousness, and shock of seeing a foreign leader in these circumstances, some people online have sidestepped the politics and seized upon the image itself, in order to talk about the clothing."

The Times did not immediately respond to Fox News Digital's request for comment.

The U.S. military launched strikes against Venezuela and captured Maduro on Jan. 3 — emerging from the operation largely unscathed as it handicapped Venezuela’s defense systems and potentially conducted cyber operations against Caracas.

Maduro is awaiting trial on federal drug trafficking and weapons charges.

Altogether, more than 150 aircraft — including U.S. bombers and fighter jets — were involved in the operation, successfully completing a "large-scale strike" against Venezuela, according to Trump. Additionally, Caracas, Venezuela, suffered power outages early Jan. 3 — an indication of a potential cyber operation.

FAMILIES SUE MADURO IN US, ACCUSE EX-PRESIDENT OF DIRECTING POLICE UNIT TIED TO EXTRAJUDICIAL KILLINGS

The Times' list included Stephen Colbert, whose "Late Show" on CBS ended in May, as well as several political figures.

Health and Human Services (HHS) Secretary RFK Jr., New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani's wife, Rama Duwaji, were included as well.

The list also pointed to Second Lady Usha Vance, White House press secretary Karoline Leavitt, and Katie Miller, a podcast host and wife of Stephen Miller, the deputy chief of staff for policy and homeland security advisor in the Trump White House.

The Times listed Miller, Vance and Leavitt in one category titled, "Pregnant Women in the Trump Sphere."

"It’s a potent image for an administration that has made clear its position that women should be having more children. These three women — Usha Vance, Katie Miller and Karoline Leavitt — create a portrait of idealized femininity, the counterpart to the masculine bravado put forth by the men of the White House," the Times wrote.

The outlet's list also included a range of actors, podcast hosts, foreign leaders, athletes and New York Knicks fans.
